headline: Scientists Discover New Cat Species, Hint at Six More Waiting
meta_description: A newly described cat species from Bolivia's cloud forests signals a genetic revolution in feline taxonomy, with researchers expecting several more species to…
summary_short: Scientists have formally described the tilcayo, a spotted cat from Bolivia discovered after more than a century without a new living cat species. Genetic research sugges…
body:
For the first time in over 100 years, scientists have formally described a previously unknown living cat species: the tilcayo (Leopardus tilcayo), a small spotted cat from Bolivia's Yungas cloud forests. But this discovery is just the beginning. Genetic analysis shows the tilcayo's lineage diverged from other tiger cats around 1.4 million years ago—and researchers now believe it may be one of many overlooked feline species awaiting recognition. According to Tadeu Gomes de Oliveira, a Brazilian wildlife biologist and co-chair of the IUCN Species Survival Commission Cat Specialist Group, the tiger-cat complex alone could expand from three recognized species to as many as six or seven. The implications stretch far beyond taxonomy. When a population gains official species status, it becomes eligible for targeted conservation funding and legal protection. Oliveira points to the munoai pampas cat as a cautionary example: he estimates only about 200 individuals remain in the wild. "If the pampas cat is not split, munoai is doomed," Oliveira explained in a recent interview. "Formal species recognition is the key to unlocking focused conservation efforts and funding."

The discovery reflects a broader revolution in understanding small wild cats of the Americas. Several populations once classified as regional subspecies are now recognized—or proposed—as distinct species based on emerging genetic research. Researchers are also reassessing the taxonomy of margays and other small cats, suggesting the full extent of feline diversity has been significantly underestimated.

This recognition comes amid renewed commitment to small cat conservation. The Ayers Wild Cat Conservation Trust committed at least $20 million over a decade to wild cat work through Panthera's Global Alliance for Wild Cats, with particular emphasis on small species that have historically received far less attention than their larger cousins. As the field embraces this genetic revolution, conservationists hope formal species descriptions will finally give overlooked cats the protection they deserve.
quick_facts: Tilcayo is first new living cat species described in more than 100 years
Tiger-cat group could expand from 3 to 6 or 7 recognized species
Only approximately 200 munoai pampas cats estimated to remain
Bolivia's Yungas cloud forests where tilcayo was discovered
$20 million committed to small wild cat conservation over 10 years
